speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To understand the underlying cause, where exactly did you first notice these symptoms, and how long have they been progressing?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Subacute Combined Degeneration of the Spinal Cord. The combination of progressive gait ataxia, lower limb weakness, and cognitive/psychiatric changes over months in a 44-year-old male is highly suggestive of Vitamin B12 deficiency, likely due to pernicious anemia or dietary factors. I need to confirm this with specific lab work. REQUEST TEST: Vitamin B12 level, Complete Blood Count (CBC), and Methylmalonic acid (MMA). REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical and Thoracic Spine MRI to rule out structural causes like a tumor or syrinx.
